name: How to Tackle a Stubborn Smelly Drain

step.name: Step 1
step.text: A foul-smelling drain is one of those annoying household issues that can really bring down the vibe of your home. When you've tried the usual tricks like pouring hot water or a baking soda and vinegar mix, and that nasty odor just won't budge, it's time to get a bit more strategic. First, make sure you're cleaning any visible gunk from the drain stopper or cover; sometimes, that's all it takes. For kitchen drains, consider cleaning your garbage disposal thoroughly – grind up some ice, rock salt, and citrus peels to freshen it up and scrape away grime. If the smell persists, you might have a dried-out P-trap, especially in a little-used sink. A P-trap holds a small amount of water to block sewer gases from coming up. Simply run water for a minute or two to refill it. However, if none of these DIY solutions work, or if you're experiencing slow drainage along with the smell, it's a strong indicator of a deeper clog or vent pipe issue. These problems usually need specialized tools like drain snakes or hydro-jetting equipment to properly clear. Trying to force a blockage out yourself can sometimes push it further down or even damage your pipes. That's when professional help becomes really important.
